subject: Post-call: Finosys discovery — cost drivers, batching & quantization openness
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@finosys.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood-inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Finosys discovery — cost drivers, batching & quantization openness

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Key pain points you shared
- Token/unit costs with current hosted provider are a hard blocker for feature expansion (esp. for nightly batch reports).
- Peak windows (analytics refresh at 03:00 PST) create unacceptable tail latency and drive up unit economics.
- Ops overhead: maintaining custom batching logic + cache invalidation across services.

Current stack you mentioned
- Frontend -> backend services -> hosted LLM API (pay-per-token) for both sync chat and async report generation.
- Traffic: ~120M tokens/day average, single-hour peaks up to ~1.2M tokens/hour during nightly jobs.
- Some internal compliance requirements (data residency, audit logs) for finance workloads.

Success criteria (what would make a pilot successful)
- 2.5x–3x reduction in per-token served cost vs. current provider for the report pipeline (including infra + token costs).
- P95 latency for interactive flows <= 400ms. For nightly reports, allow up to +200ms average latency if it improves batch efficiency and reduces cost significantly.
- No >5% perceived quality regression on canonical prompts (we'll provide a small eval set).

Technical openness and constraints
- You said the team is open to model quantization (4-bit / int4) if it preserves quality on your eval set.
- Happy to test batching and prefix/KV caching; you indicated a willingness to accept a small tail latency increase for batching gains during non-peak interactive windows.

Proposed next steps
1) You share a telemetry sample (we requested a CSV with 48 hours of request traces + sample prompts). We can use this to simulate batching/caching impact and estimate unit economics. (Attachment requested.)
2) We’ll run a short synthetic simulation + a small on-prem pilot (or dedicated capacity) to model cost at your traffic profile — target delivery in 7 business days after we have telemetry.
3) Exchange a simple mutual action plan (I attached a draft) with owners, timeline, and success metrics.
4) We’ll include SOC 2 scope and a short compliance checklist for the pilot.

Attachments: finosys-inference-telemetry-sample.csv (placeholder you can upload), finosys-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft).

Open questions for you
- Can you confirm whether the 1.2M token/hour peak is sustained for >30 minutes or short spikes?
- Are there any internal rules that prohibit us from using quantized model variants in your staging environment?

I’ll follow up with a short scope doc and simulated cost delta once I have the telemetry. If this looks right, can we schedule a 30-min technical kickoff the week of May 24th?

Thanks — Karthik

--

Subject: Re: Post-call: Finosys discovery — cost drivers, batching & quantization openness

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side: useful summary.

Confirmations
- The 1.2M token/hour peak is generally a 45–90 minute sustained window during our ETL/report runs. It's not a 10-minute burst.
- We are comfortable trying quantized variants in staging (security team wants a quick quality/regression sweep and we need audit logs retained).
- Compliance: SOC 2 report and data residency confirmation will be required before production sign-off (staging pilot OK with standard confidentiality protections).

Asks from Finosys
- Can you give a ballpark cost delta (per 1M tokens) for a dedicated pilot vs. our current hosted provider? Even a back-of-envelope is helpful to set internal expectations.
- Timeline: we can commit to a 4-week pilot window starting June 7th if mutual action plan and billing terms are acceptable.
- Please include any relevant contract redlines we should expect (IP/data handling, encryption, retention).

I've attached the quick telemetry extract you asked for (see finosys-inference-telemetry-sample.csv). Let me know if you need more fields. Also attached is our internal compliance checklist (not included in thread).

Appreciate the proposed pilot approach. Monica (cc) will be the technical lead on our side.

—Emma
